slides.title:
Removing Microplastics
with Sand-Biofilm Filters
slides.subtitle: A low-cost filtration design for small coastal treatment plants — thesis defense, Noura Al-Harbi.
slides.notes: Introduce yourself, program, supervisors. One sentence on why this matters locally.

slides.title: Defense roadmap
slides.notes: Roadmap reduces panel cognitive load. Mention backup slides exist for detail questions.

slides.title: Coastal plants discharge microplastics untreated

bullets.head: Secondary treatment misses small particles
bullets.body: Particles under 300 micrometers pass conventional clarifiers largely intact.

bullets.head: Membrane upgrades are unaffordable locally
bullets.body: Capex and energy costs exceed small-plant budgets by 4-6x.

bullets.head: Biofilm-sand hybrids are understudied
bullets.body: No published data for Red Sea salinity and temperature ranges.

slides.visual_caption: Particle size below which conventional treatment stops working.
slides.notes: Establish the gap: effective + affordable + local conditions. Cite sources verbally.

slides.title: Three questions this thesis answers

items.head: Salinity effect?
items.body: Does Red Sea salinity degrade biofilm performance?

items.head: Operating cost?
items.body: Can OPEX stay under $0.05 per cubic meter?

slides.notes: Panels grade conclusions against these exact questions. Pause here.

slides.title: Pilot rig ran 112 days across three salinities

steps.head: Build
steps.body: Three 200L columns: sand, biofilm-sand, membrane control.

steps.head: Seed
steps.body: Biofilm cultured 21 days on local seawater inoculum.

steps.head: Run
steps.body: 112 days at 35 / 40 / 45 ppt, weekly particle counts.

steps.head: Measure
steps.body: FTIR-verified counts in 4 size bands, triplicate samples.

slides.notes: Flowchart beats bullets for methods. Mention triplication and FTIR verification unprompted.

slides.title: Biofilm-sand removed 93% — near membrane performance
slides.insight: Biofilm-sand reaches 93% removal vs 97% for membrane — at roughly one-fifth of the operating cost. The 4-point gap is the price of affordability.
slides.notes: Answer RQ1 explicitly: yes, above the 90% threshold at all salinities tested.

slides.label: Operating cost of the biofilm-sand design
slides.context: vs $0.21/m³ membrane benchmark — inside the RQ3 target
slides.notes: STAR moment. Let it breathe 3 seconds, then answer RQ3.

slides.title: Salinity slowed start-up, not steady performance

bullets.head: 45 ppt delayed biofilm maturity 9 days
bullets.body: Steady-state removal equalized after day 40 at all salinities.

bullets.head: Backwash cycle is the main OPEX driver
bullets.body: Optimizing backwash timing is the clearest cost lever.

bullets.head: Limitation: single polymer mix tested
bullets.body: Polyester fibers dominated; tire-wear particles untested.

slides.visual_caption: Days to steady state at the highest salinity.
slides.notes: Name limitations before the panel does — credibility. Backup slide has salinity curves.

slides.title: Affordable removal is achievable
slides.ask: Recommendation: pilot at plant scale (10 m³/day) with backwash optimization as phase two.
